raw_text:
Here’s a detailed 12-week postpartum return-to-training program for a 33-year-old client, four weeks post uncomplicated cesarean section, cleared for light activity (walking, no abs, no heavy lifting) with a home setup (yoga mat only). The plan progresses gradually from gentle mobilization and posture work toward foundational strength, then controlled loading, and finally basic return-to-activity conditioning. Each week includes a weekly structure, session-by-session details, exercise selections, sets/reps, and recovery/nutrition notes. All movements are low load, focusing on core re-engagement, diastasis-safe breathing, pelvic floor activation, and gradual tissue loading. If any movement causes pain (especially back, pelvic floor, or incision area), stop and consult a clinician.

Important notes and safety
- Check-in points: If you have any symptoms (pelvic organ prolapse, persistent diastasis >2-3 cm at rest, severe pelvic/abdominal pain, heavy bleeding), pause progress and consult your OB/PT.
- Core strategy: focus on gentle diaphragmatic breathing, pelvic floor engagement, and progressively loading the transverse and deep core muscles without doing traditional crunches or heavy abdominal work.
- Diastasis awareness: avoid full abdominal closure crunches; normalize intra-abdominal pressure with breath work and braced, low-load activation.
- Movement readiness: since four weeks post-C-section, avoid high-impact, heavy lifting, or abdominal bracing that strains the incision. Keep workouts on a mat with a focus on alignment.
- Progression principle: add volume first (sets/reps), then tempo, then light resistance if applicable, while maintaining technique and core control.
- Nutrition and recovery: aim for protein intake around 1.2–1.6 g/kg body weight per day, adequate hydration, and prioritize sleep and rest. Consider a small protein-rich snack post-workout and a balanced plate at meals. If breastfed, ensure hydration and energy needs are met.

Weekly structure overview
- Frequency: 4 days/week (adjustable for client schedule).
- Focus: Week 1–4 emphasize gentle mobility, diaphragmatic breathing, pelvic floor activation, and light glute/hamstring engagement. Weeks 5–8 introduce more foundational strength with low-load resistance and controlled tempo. Weeks 9–12 introduce conditioning and more functional movements with continued core protection. Throughout, no crunches or sit-ups; no heavy lifting; avoid abdominal bracing that strains the incision.

Weeks 1–4: Establishing a safe foundation (gentle mobility, breathing, pelvic floor, glutes)
Goal: Reestablish mind-muscle connection, pelvic floor control, and basic hip stability; build consistency.

Session structure: 4 sessions per week (A/B alternating). Each session 20–35 minutes.

Week 1
- Session A (20–25 min): Breath + Pelvic Floor + Glute Activation
  1) Diaphragmatic breathing with pelvic floor activation: 2 sets x 6 breaths (inhale nose, exhale mouth, on exhale gently lift pelvic floor) – 1 min rest between
  2) Quadruped pelvis tilts (cat-camel with neutral spine): 2 sets x 8 reps
  3) Glute bridge (bodyweight, feet hip-width, neutral spine): 2–3 sets x 10 reps, slow tempo 3–0-3
  4) Side-lying clamshells (no resistance, if comfortable): 2 sets x 12 reps per side
  5) Dead bug regressions (hands/knees, reach opposite arm/leg only to neutral, keep spine stable): 2 sets x 6 reps per side

- Session B (25–30 min): Mobility + Postural Work
  1) Wall roll-downs to neutral spine (gentle): 2 sets x 6
  2) Hip hinge into a chair stance (mini-squat progressions without actual squats): 2 sets x 8
  3) Glute bridge hold at top: 2 x 15–20 sec
  4) Seated thoracic mobility (with towel behind back): 2 x 1 min
  5) Pelvic floor + transverse activation: 2 sets x 8 reps (hold 2–3 sec per rep)

Week 2
- Session A (25–30 min): Core/Pelvic Floor Progression
  1) Diaphragmatic breathing with longer exhale: 2 sets x 8 breaths
  2) Quadruped opposite limb extension (contralateral arm/leg) – keep pelvis stable: 2–3 sets x 6 reps per side
  3) Glute bridge march (bridge with small knee march): 3 sets x 10 reps per side
  4) Side-lying hip abduction with knee bent: 2–3 sets x 12 reps per side
  5) Bird-dog regressions on all fours (slow control): 2 sets x 6 reps per side

- Session B (30–35 min): Mobility + Lower-Body Stability
  1) Hip flexor/quad stretch (gentle): 2 x 30–45 sec per side
  2) Seated single-leg hip hinge (posterior chain focus): 2–3 sets x 8 reps per side
  3) Glute bridge hold with abduction (feet apart slightly, push hips up): 2 x 20–25 sec
  4) Dead bug progressions (opposite arm/leg with leg only): 2–3 sets x 8 reps per side
  5) Posture work: chin tucks, scapular retractions, 2 sets x 10 reps

Week 3
- Session A (30–35 min): Foundation strengthening
  1) Diaphragmatic breathing with 4–count exhale: 2 sets x 8 breaths
  2) Quadruped diagonal arm/leg with knee near mat: 3 sets x 8 reps per side
  3) Supine pelvic tilt with march: 3 sets x 12 reps
  4) Side-lying clamshells with gentle isometric hold at top: 2–3 sets x 10 reps per side
  5) Bird-dog with extended reach (moderate control): 2–3 sets x 6 reps per side

- Session B (30–40 min): Mobility + Glute/Posterior Chain Focus
  1) Hip hinge to chair (progression): 3 sets x 8 reps
  2) Hip abduction standing (hold onto chair): 2–3 sets x 12 reps per side
  3) Glute bridge with march and hold at top: 2–3 sets x 10 reps per side
  4) Seated thoracic rotation: 2 sets x 8 reps per side
  5) Pelvic floor activation with breathing drill: 2 sets x 8 reps

Week 4
- Session A (35 min): Early Resistance Introduction (low load)
  1) Diaphragmatic breathing with extended exhale and gentle core bracing (non-clam): 2 sets x 8 breaths
  2) Glute bridge with light tempo (2–0–2): 3 sets x 12 reps
  3) Standing hip hinge (light activation, no weight): 3 sets x 10 reps
  4) Supine wall-assisted dead bug: 2–3 sets x 8 reps per side
  5) Postural/pelvic alignment flow: 5 minutes, dynamic stretches

- Session B (35–40 min): Core Activation + Mobility
  1) Diaphragm breathing with 5–6 sec exhale: 2 sets x 8 breaths
  2) Quadruped opposite limb drill with controlled tempo: 3 sets x 6 reps per side
  3) Hip bridge with isometric hold at top: 3 x 15–20 sec
  4) Side-lying leg lift (abduct): 2–3 sets x 12 reps per side
  5) Cat-camel + thoracic mobility sequence: 3 rounds

Progression note for Weeks 1–4: The emphasis is to restore basic neuromuscular control, pelvic floor function, and gluteal activation without imposing abdominal strain. If any incision discomfort occurs, reduce range or scale back and maintain breathing work.

Weeks 5–8: Building foundational strength and safe loading
Goal: Introduce gentle resistance and controlled loading while preserving core and pelvic floor integrity. Sessions move toward 4 days/week, still mat-based with emphasis on posture and diaphragmatic breathing.

Week 5
- Session A (30–40 min): Lower-Body Primers
  1) Diaphragmatic breathing with 4–count exhale: 2 sets x 8 breaths
  2) Hip hinge with resistance band (or bodyweight if no band): 3 sets x 12 reps
  3) Glute bridge with tempo 3–0–3: 3 sets x 12 reps
  4) Standing hip abduction (light tension, 12–15 reps per side): 2–3 sets
  5) Plank progression prep (on knees, if tolerable): 2 sets x 10–15 sec

- Session B (30–40 min): Core Integration
  1) Diaphragmatic breathing with breath holds (very light): 2 sets x 6 breaths
  2) Side-lying clamshells with tiny resistance (mini-band if available): 3 sets x 12 reps per side
  3) Dead bug with pause at dead center: 3 sets x 8 reps per side
  4) Glute bridge with single-leg march (alternate legs): 3 sets x 8 reps per side
  5) Hip mobility sequence: 5 minutes

Week 6
- Session A (35–45 min): Introduce Light Loading
  1) Diaphragmatic breathing with longer exhale + brace as tolerated: 2 sets x 8 breaths
  2) Hip hinge with light resistance band: 3 sets x 12 reps
  3) Glute bridge with tempo and small pause at top: 3 sets x 12 reps
  4) Prone or supine isometric core activation (gentle, no strain): 2 sets x 15–20 sec
  5) Pelvic floor activation with glute engagement sequence: 2–3 sets

- Session B (35–45 min): Upper-Body Preparatory Movements (bodyweight)
  1) Scapular retraction rows (using a towel or doorway as resistance): 3 sets x 10–12 reps
  2) Wall push-up progressions (hands on wall, elbow depth 45–60 degrees): 3 sets x 8–10 reps
  3) Pallof ish (anti-rotation) with light resistance or towel drag: 2–3 sets x 8 reps per side
  4) Glute bridge with march + reach (arm reach forward on mat): 3 sets x 10 reps per side
  5) Mobility finish: hip/quad/shoulder

Week 7
- Session A (40–50 min): Controlled Load
  1) Diaphragmatic breathing with braced core: 2 sets x 8 breaths
  2) Hip hinge to chair with light resistance band: 3–4 sets x 10–12 reps
  3) Glute bridge with single-leg progression (unsupported if comfortable): 3 sets x 8 reps per side
  4) Bird-dog with extended reach (control): 3 sets x 8 reps per side
  5) Side-lying hip abduction with tempo: 2–3 sets x 12–15 reps

- Session B (40–50 min): Core-Ready
  1) Dead bug with hold: 3 sets x 8–10 reps per side
  2) Supine dead bug with leg lowering (only small ROM): 3 sets x 8 reps
  3) Seated rows with towel (scapular emphasis): 3 sets x 12 reps
  4) Glute bridge with hold at top + pulse: 3 sets x 12–15 sec
  5) Mobility circuit: 5–7 minutes

Week 8
- Session A (45–55 min): Light Resistance + Posture
  1) Diaphragmatic breathing with 3–5 sec pause: 2 sets x 8 breaths
  2) Hip hinge with resistance band banded pull-apart: 3 sets x 12 reps
  3) Glute bridge with alternating single-leg support: 3 sets x 8 reps per side
  4) Clamshells with mini-band: 3 sets x 12 reps per side
  5) Prone scapular stabilization with chin tuck: 2–3 sets x 10 reps

- Session B (45–55 min): Lower-Body Stability
  1) Wall-assisted split squats (mini-range): 3 sets x 8 reps per side
  2) Step-back taps (no load) with hip hinge: 3 sets x 10 reps per side
  3) Glute bridge with tempo and hold: 3 sets x 12 reps
  4) Bird-dog with knee-to-elbow crunch replaced by safe control: 3 sets x 8 reps
  5) Mobility flow: 6–8 minutes

Weeks 9–12: Return to more functional activity and conditioning
Goal: Build capacity with more structured, progressive loading while preserving core integrity. Introduce gentle cardio options and more functional movements suitable for daily life and postpartum needs.

Week 9
- Session A (45–60 min): Full-Body Foundation
  1) Diaphragmatic breathing with 4-count exhale: 2 sets x 8 breaths
  2) Hip hinge with light resistance (DBs if available, otherwise bodyweight): 3–4 sets x 10–12 reps
  3) Glute bridge with tempo (2–0–2) and hold: 3 sets x 12 reps
  4) Push-up progression (knees on mat or incline using wall): 3 sets x 8–10 reps
  5) Pallof press with light resistance (short lever): 2–3 sets x 8 reps per side

- Session B (45–60 min): Conditioning Intro
  1) Low-impact cardio option: brisk walk or marching in place for 15–20 minutes total, broken into 5-minute bouts
  2) Bodyweight circuit: 2 rounds of 6–8 exercise sequence (squat to chair, shoulder tap planks on knees, hip bridge, march, side plank on knees, leg raise in dead bug position)
  3) Mobility and cooldown: 6–8 minutes

Week 10
- Session A (45–60 min): Strength Emphasis
  1) Diaphragmatic breathing during bracing: 2 sets x 8 breaths
  2) Goblet-style movement with light weight (water bottle or dumbbell if available) via hip hinge and squat pattern: 3 sets x 10–12 reps
  3) Glute bridge with pulse and hold: 3 sets x 12–15 sec
  4) Push-up progression (KNEES only to full incline as tolerated): 3 sets x 8–10 reps
  5) Side plank with knee support (if tolerable): 3 sets x 15–20 sec per side

- Session B (45–60 min): Cardio + Core Integration
  1) Low-impact cardio: 20–25 minutes brisk walk with intervals (1 min faster pace, 2 min easy pace)
  2) Core-friendly circuit: dead bug, side-lying leg lift, bird-dog, all with controlled tempo; 3 rounds
  3) Mobility: 6–8 minutes

Week 11
- Session A (50–65 min): Moderate Loading
  1) Diaphragmatic breathing + bracing sequence: 2 sets x 8–10 breaths
  2) Dumbbell deadlift to mid-shoop (if available) or heavy hinge with contraction: 3–4 sets x 8–12 reps
  3) Split squat progression (supported or hands-free depending): 3 sets x 8–10 reps per side
  4) Glute bridge with single-leg reach: 3 sets x 8 reps per side
  5) Plank on knees or incline: 3 sets x 20–30 sec

- Session B (50–65 min): Conditioning Focus
  1) Cardio intervals: 25–30 minutes of low-impact intervals (bike or walk incline, if available; otherwise walking)
  2) Core control circuit: 3 rounds
  3) Mobility and breathwork: 7–10 minutes

Week 12
- Session A (60 min): Return-to-Activity Readiness
  1) Full-body circuit: 3 rounds of 8–10 reps per exercise
     - Goblet squat (light weight) or chair squat
     - Hip hinge pattern with dumbbell if available
     - Glute bridge with march
     - Bent-over row with light towel
     - Plank on knees or incline as tolerated
  2) Finisher: 5–7 minutes of light cardio (marching, step-ups if available)
  3) Cool-down: 6–8 minutes

- Session B (60 min): Conditioning and Maintenance
  1) Cardio: 25–30 minutes moderate-intensity steady state (walking, cycling with low resistance, or jog/walk if cleared)
  2) Mobility and core: 15–20 minutes focusing on hip flexor, thoracic rotation, and diaphragmatic breathing
  3) Post-workout nutrition alignment: balance meals and hydration

Nutrition and recovery notes
- Protein target: 1.2–1.6 g/kg body weight per day to support recovery and tissue repair. Include a protein-rich source with every meal.
- Hydration: Aim for at least 2.0–2.5 liters per day, more if breastfeeding.
- Sleep and stress: Prioritize sleep and rest when possible; short naps can help recovery.
- Post-workout nutrition: A small protein-rich snack within 1–2 hours after workouts (e.g., yogurt with berries, a smoothie with protein, or a piece of cheese and fruit) supports muscle recovery.
- Supplements: Continue prenatal vitamins as advised by OB. Consider vitamin D and omega-3 if dietary intake is low, after discussing with clinician.

Return-to-exercise progression guidelines
- Use a RPE (perceived exertion) target of 3–4/10 in weeks 1–4, 4–5/10 in weeks 5–8, and 5–6/10 by weeks 9–12 for most exercises.
- If diastasis recti is present or worsens, avoid traditional abdominal bracing and any movement that bulges the abdomen. Focus on diaphragmatic breathing and pelvic floor engagement until cleared.
- Incision area: avoid any exercise that causes pulling or strain around the C-section incision. Scale back intensity and range as needed.

Equipment and exercise substitutions
- If you gain access to light resistance bands or dumbbells, substitute bodyweight movements with bands for progressive overload (e.g., banded hip hinge, band-resisted rows).
- If only a mat is available, all exercises can be done with bodyweight; progress by tempo, range of motion, and sets/reps rather than load.

Please note: This plan is a blueprint. Monitor her response weekly, adjust intensity based on comfort, incision healing, and clinician guidance at the six-week check. If you want, I can tailor the program to her current equipment availability (e.g., bands, dumbbells) and adjust weekly volumes to match her recovery pace and schedule.
